Low 42° Mean 51° Record High 87° Record High Date Mar 26th, 1921 Record Low 23° Record Low Date Mar 26th, 1955 Full Weather Report Last updated on March 26, 2026 at 4:51 a.m. Eileen Whelan, 7News First Alert Meteorologist TODAY: Partly sunny, breezy Highs: 74-80 Winds: Southwest 5-15, Gusts 25 mph The cherry blossoms may reach peak bloom with the warm weather, so it will be a great day to see the pink petals.Plan for high temperatures to soar to around 80 degrees; which is 20-degrees above normal for late March. Breezy southwest winds will increase later today ahead of a strong cold front that will bring changes tomorrow. Until then, plan for a mix of sun and clouds throughout the day with a stray shower or sprinkle not out of the question. Very warm weather is expected this evening with temperatures in the 70s. TONIGHT: Mostly cloudy Showers by dawn Temps: 70s to 60s Winds: Southwest 10-15+ mph It will be very warm overnight with temperatures slowly falling from the 70s into the 60s. It will remain breezy ahead of the cold front. Rain will develop from north to south during the overnight hours. Showers will likely make it the MD/PA state line between 3-4 a.m. with rain inside the Beltway by 5 a.m. FRIDAY: Rain likely, breezy Falling Temperatures Temps: 60s to 50s Winds: North 5-15, Gusts to 25 mph Friday turns unsettled as a strong cold front slowly pushes across the DMV, bringing widespread showers and perhaps a rumble of thunder, especially early in the day. The severe weather threat drops off quickly by the time the line reaches the DC area, so while rain is likely, the risk for severe storms in Washington looks limited at this time. Showers may linger into the afternoon before conditions gradually improve from north to south later in the day. The damp, gray weather will not make for the best cherry blossom viewing around the Tidal Basin, but the bigger story will be the cooler air arriving by evening. SATURDAY: Mostly sunny Highs: 47-52 Winds: Northwest 10-15 mph Cold temperatures in the lower 30s will start the weekend, and Saturday will feel noticeably cooler as Canadian high pressure builds in behind the front. Highs will only reach the mid 40s to low 50s, and the air will feel crisp and dry. It should be a bright day overall, though definitely jacket weather if you are heading to the Tidal Basin. SUNDAY: Sunny and beautiful Highs: 59-64 Winds: Southwest 5-10 mph Sunday brings a modest warm-up as high pressure shifts offshore and southerly flow returns. Temperatures rebound into the upper 50s and 60s, making it a more comfortable day across the DC area with dry weather continuing. It looks like a much nicer day to get outside and enjoy the cherry blossoms around the Tidal Basin, with a more seasonable spring feel returning by the end of the weekend. 7 News First Alert Weather Veronica Johnson Chief Meteorologist Jordan Evans Meteorologist Mark Peña Meteorologist Steve Rudin Meteorologist Brian Van de Graaff Senior Meteorologist More from WTOP
